messages:
devsec-bot: detection: sso.geo-velocity + refresh-reuse signature triggered for ~18 accounts in a 12m window (EU -> NA rapid hops). flag: possible session replay / token replay.

anya: ack. which accounts? any admin roles impacted?

mike: pulling list now. majority are end-user, 3 service accounts, 1 infra-admin. user-agent looks identical across events, token ids show multiple distinct IPs using the same refresh token id. not standard credential stuffing.

sara: creating incident: INC-4062, severity = P0 due to admin involvement and customer lockouts. notifying CS & legal.

claire: containment checklist: 1) revoke active sessions for impacted accounts (cookie/session store) 2) invalidate refresh tokens (provider-side revoke or rotate client secret) 3) enforce step-up (MFA) for any privileged roles that saw attempts. ops, can you run revokes?

ops: running bulk session revokes. note: our admin revoke only removes sessions issued by us; it may not invalidate provider-issued refresh tokens. command: ```adminctl sessions revoke --emails "alice@acme.com,bob@acme.com,..." --all```

mike: thanks. big caveat: if refresh tokens remain valid they can mint new sessions. we should do a targeted oauth client secret rotate for affected org(s). avoid rotating global client unless absolutely necessary. command we will use: ```oauth-client rotate-secret --org acme --targeted```

anya: agree, targeted rotate only. ops, coordinate with eng-auth for token introspection to ensure refresh IDs are logged and marked revoked.

eng-auth: we can add temporary token-introspect middleware to reject refresh token ids that show reuse across >2 geos within 1h. will push rule as a short-lived mitigation.

claire: also add an immediate rate limit on MFA push attempts (e.g., max 3 pushes / 10m per account) to reduce MFA fatigue attacks.

ops: revokes returned 200. starting targeted oauth-client rotate for the 3 affected orgs now. ETA ~18m. documenting change in audit log.

mike: KMS/cloud key note: no unusual decrypt requests in cloud-kms logs for keys used by auth service in last 24h. exporting full KMS access log to sec-bucket for review.

sara: CS outreach: we've sent emails to impacted customers explaining forced re-auth and recommended credential checks. legal standing by; will escalate if evidence of exfiltration.

devsec-bot: artifacts queued: SSO assertion dumps, refresh token IDs, IP CIDR list, UA hashes, KMS access logs, oauth client rotate audit entries.

claire: post-containment, we need these follow-ups: 1) add a permanent detector for refresh-token reuse signature, 2) tighten RBAC for client secret rotations (2-person approval), 3) increase audit retention for KMS and token audit logs to 90 days, 4) tabletop in 10 days. I'll open tickets.

anya: ops/eng-auth: confirm targeted rotate completed and whether failed refresh attempts dropped.

ops: targeted rotate finished. telemetry shows refresh reuse attempts drop to zero and new failed refreshes hitting token-introspect rule. users re-authenticating; no further admin compromises detected. containment closed.

mike: small post-action: add alert for any future client-secret rotation events and require an approver tag for rotations in the UI.

claire: updating RBAC change: require approver from infra-sre + sec lead for any client-secret rotate. adding audit webhook to post to #eng-security on rotate events.

sara: incident summary posted to #incidents; execs notified. scheduling 60m postmortem tomorrow 11:00. owners: ops (revokes/rotate), eng-auth (detectors), sec (postmortem).

legal: standing by for notification if we confirm account compromise or PII access; for now we classify as attempted session replay.

anya: create runbook entry: "refresh-token reuse -> targeted oauth-client rotate + token-introspect rule". assign to eng-auth for authoring.

devsec-bot: Post-incident checklist created.

sara: thanks team. closing channel for immediate actions. follow-ups tracked in INC-4062. :lock:
